full_judgment:
Md Mozibur Rahman Miah, J: On an application under article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order No. 23 dated 5-9-2021 (Annexure-`A' to the writ petition) passed by the respondent No. 1 in Artha Jari Case No. 06 of 2020 attaching 1,00,44,317 ordinary shares of Taka 10 each belonging to the respondent No. 5-judgment-debtor in the petitioner-bank in favour of the respondent No. 2-decree-holder-bank in satisfaction of the decree, disregarding the plea that the said shares have earlier been pledged in favour of the petitioner-bank should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 The present respondent No. 2 as plaintiff originally filed a suit being Artha Rin Suit No. 127 of 2012 against the present respondent No. 5 and another claiming an amount of Taka 28,49,05,028.41. In the suit, the present respondent No. 5 as defendant No. 2 entered appearance and contested the same. Ultimately, the respondent No. 1 by his judgment and order dated 28-8-2019 decreed the suit on contest. To execute the decree, the respondent No. 2 then filed an execution case being Artha Execution Case No. 06 of 2020 claiming an amount of Taka 53,40,67,641.41. In course of the said execution case, the decree-holder-respondent No. 2, Southeast Bank Ltd. on 9-3-2021 filed an application for attaching 1,00,44,317 shares so mentioned in the schedule of the application contending that, the market value of those shares is Taka 10,04,43,170 held by the respondent No. 5. The petitioner, Standard Bank Ltd. as applicant then on 16-3-2021 filed an application under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain praying for rejecting the said application of the decree-holder-bank asserting that those shares are already in pledged with it (the petitioner) and it cannot be attached by the decree-holder-respondent No. 2 and prayed for rejecting the application. However, against the application for rejection filed by the petitioner dated 16-3-2021, the respondent No 2 filed written objection on 22-3-2021 (photocopy of the certified copy of the same has been supplied by the learned counsel for the respondent No. 2 during hearing of the Rule) alleging inter alia that, since the petitioner is a third party so such application cannot be entertained under section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. It has also been asserted in the written objection that, as per section 27(1) of the Bank Company Act, 1991, the respondent No. 5 cannot avail any loan facilities by pledging his own share lying with his bank. It has further been stated therein that, since the respondent No. 2 obtained a decree so to execute the decree, the shares of the petitioner should be attached. 

 12. The learned counsel next contends that, as per section 26 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 procedure followed in executing a money decree filed under the provision of Code of Civil Procedure will equally be applicable in executing a decree filed under Artha Rin Adalat Ain provided it is not inconsistent with the former and in such a view of such legal scheme provision of order 21, rule 46 of the Code of Civil Procedure will be applicable in attaching the shares belongs to the present respondent No.5 and the respondent No. 2 has thus rightly resorted so.
